Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 39-year-old male with new severe unilateral headache, mild photophobia, no focal neurological deficits, no fever/neck stiffness. Stress and poor sleep noted. Prior milder headaches.

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript):  
• Migraine without aura – high likelihood given unilateral pain, photophobia, stress trigger.  
• Tension-type headache – moderate likelihood due to work stress and history of anxiety; atypical severity/unilaterality.  
• Cluster headache – low-moderate likelihood (early-morning unilateral pain) but lacks autonomic features.  

Red-flag considerations (low likelihood but must exclude): thunderclap/subarachnoid hemorrhage, intracranial mass (no current evidence of these).

Working diagnosis: Probable migraine without aura; tension component possible.

Management Plan

- Pharmacologic: commence Ibuprofen (high-dose per migraine guideline; exact dose not documented) and may continue Paracetamol as needed.  
- Non-pharmacologic: advise minimum 7–8 hrs sleep nightly; fluid intake 1.5–2 L water/day (exclude caffeinated drinks); consider 1 week off work (self-certify) to reduce stress.  
- Mental health: provide self-referral link to local counseling service; encourage use for stress/anxiety support.  
- Education: provide written information on headache “danger signs” and when to seek urgent care.  
- Follow-up: telephone or in-person review in one week; earlier review if headache worsens or new symptoms develop.

- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Follow-up headache review booked; other preventive items not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Migraine without aura – High likelihood: unilateral severe pain, photophobia, stress/sleep deprivation trigger, prior episodic headaches.  
2. Tension-type (stress-related) headache – Moderate likelihood: significant work stress and anxiety; previous frontal band-like headaches.  
3. Cluster headache – Low-moderate likelihood: early-morning unilateral pain, male age 39; lacks autonomic signs.
